checked_obligation: Under the predecessor assumption that a is a primitive root modulo the prime p, verify that a^((p-1)/2) is congruent to -1 modulo p.
reason: A primitive root a modulo p has order p-1, so a^(p-1)≡1 modulo p while a^((p-1)/2)≢1 modulo p because 0<(p-1)/2<p-1. Factoring a^(p-1)-1 and using primality of p gives a^((p-1)/2)≡1 or -1 modulo p; the first case is excluded, proving the claim.
